concerns.text: Task T016 explicitly removes API fetch logic ('Note: API fetch is removed...') and relies solely on synthetic data. This violates FR-001 which mandates downloading real data from Materials Project API and Inoue's compilation. The Plan's 'Critical Data Contingency' allows synthetic fallback ONLY if API fails, but the task hardcodes the removal of the API attempt, silently weakening the requirement to 'synthetic only'.

Task T027 hardcodes 'Corrected Resampled t-test' as the PRIMARY method and relegates Wilcoxon to a fallback based on Shapiro-Wilk. FR-007 requires 'corrected resampled t-test OR paired permutation test'. The task omits the 'paired permutation test' option entirely, violating the spec's authorized comparison methods.

Task T035 instructs to use a 'sufficient number of permutations' without specifying the count. FR-009 and US-3 explicitly require '100 permutations'. This semantic weakening allows the implementation to deviate from the fixed resource constraint and statistical power defined in the spec.

Task T019 introduces complex conditional logic (VIF > 5 triggers iterative removal, then PCA, then Ridge fallback) not authorized in FR-003. FR-003 only requires computing descriptors. This constitutes scope creep and a silent relaxation of the data hygiene principle by introducing unverified model-training logic into the feature engineering phase.

Tasks T020 and T031 implement logic to exclude families with <10 samples from the test set or switch to GroupKFold only if >50% of families are small. This contradicts FR-008 (LOFO) and the Plan's 'Complexity Tracking' which aims to test generalization across ALL families. This silently drops data segments the spec intended to validate.
